### Summary
Adds the `mentalModelAndModels` variation to the V2 new-session onboarding tour (`sessions.onboarding.newSessionViewV2`):

- **Spotlight `selectedContent` support**: Allows `ISpotlightStep` to specify `selectedContent` (`title` and `description`) that replaces the step's default copy when the target already has a selected value (`hasOnboardingTargetSelection`), matching `openTarget: 'ifUnselected'`.
- **`mentalModelAndModels` variation**: Preserves the 2-step `workspaceAndModel` flow (`workspacePicker` -> `modelPicker`) while updating the copy for users coming from the classic VS Code editor window:
  - **Workspace picker (unselected)**: *"Pick a project for this session"* — *"Unlike a normal VS Code window, you aren't locked to one folder. Point this session at any repo or folder—or switch projects anytime without opening a new window."*
  - **Workspace picker (preselected)**: *"Pick a project for this session"* — *"We've selected your current project to get you started. You can point each new session at any repo or folder—all from this window."*
  - **Model picker**: *"All your favorite models, one place"* — *"Claude, GPT, Gemini, and more—the best models from across the industry are ready to go. Pick your favorite or switch anytime."*

### Validation
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/onboarding/browser/spotlight/spotlightTypes.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/onboarding/browser/spotlight/spotlightPresentation.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/onboardingTours/browser/tours/newSessionViewV2Tour.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/onboardingTours/browser/newSessionViewV2TourVariation.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/onboarding/test/browser/spotlightPresentation.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/onboardingTours/test/browser/newSessionViewV2Tour.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/onboardingTours/test/browser/onboardingTourDescriptors.test.ts` — passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/onboarding/test/browser/spotlightPresentation.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/onboardingTours/test/browser/newSessionViewV2Tour.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/onboardingTours/test/browser/onboardingTourDescriptors.test.ts` — passed (60 passing)

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench restoration and registration of the V2 new-session onboarding tour
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The AfterRestored contribution constructs the trigger and registers a scenario. The added variation payload, localized strings, and lookup table are allocated during module evaluation, but no variation resolution or remote assignment lookup occurs until the scenario actually runs.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant: one contribution, three static payloads, and a fixed set of two or three steps per workbench window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous contribution registration; no queue, burst, or parallel work is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache. Existing storage/configuration eligibility reads are unchanged; the static payload objects remain module-scoped for the window lifetime just as the existing payloads did.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the contribution and module-level payload construction are directly visible, and no changed code invokes an external boundary on this path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact module-evaluation allocation is not measured, but the diff adds only a fixed handful of short strings and objects, so it cannot scale with repositories, sessions, or user data.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the PR adds only constant, small eager allocations after workbench restoration and does not move filesystem, IPC, subprocess, database, or network work onto startup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Eligible user opens the new-session view and the tour resolves its experiment variation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Before the spotlight can render, resolveSteps awaits resolveNewSessionViewV2TourVariation. With treatments enabled, this awaits one assignment-service getTreatment call; the PR then performs a three-element includes check and one static record lookup. The same treatment await was already on this critical path before the PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize/fetch shared TAS experiment assignments when the assignment service is cold, then read the new-session variation treatment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the existing shared service initialization/fetch, followed by one treatment read for this tour; not one request per variation or step.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The previous resolveVariation implementation awaited the identical getTreatment call once before selecting between default and workspaceAndModel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cold treatment read may delay resolveSteps and therefore the first spotlight, while a warm cached read does not require another fetch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Route the optional assignments endpoint request through IRequestService to the main process before the network request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Part of the same shared cold assignment fetch, not multiplied by the newly added variation or its steps.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The assignment service and this tour already used the same getTreatment path before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only relevant when the existing cold TAS setup has not completed; placement on this tour path is unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One variation resolution per triggered tour run; the trigger is one-shot after it is set or the tour has been shown. Variation cardinality increases from two to three but remains fixed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One serialized resolveSteps promise for the active tour. No per-step or per-item treatment fan-out is added, and the steps themselves are subsequently displayed serially.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: On a cold assignment service, getTreatment can await TAS client initialization and a shared initial assignment fetch; on a warm service it reads the cached treatment. This cache behavior and the single lookup key are unchanged by the diff; developer overrides still bypass the treatment read as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the call path from resolveSteps to getTreatment is explicit, and before/after both execute exactly one treatment lookup; the changed includes and record indexing are fixed-size local CPU work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold TAS duration and how often the tour races service initialization vary by environment, but neither frequency nor boundary cardinality changes in this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the only expensive boundary is pre-existing with unchanged cardinality and scheduling; the new local validation and payload lookup are constant-time at this scale.

Scenarios.Scenario: Spotlight renders workspace/model steps, including a preselected workspace and navigation back to earlier steps
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For each step that passes its context condition and resolves a visible target, _showStep now reads selection state before constructing callout content, then performs the existing overlay DOM rendering and requestAnimationFrame-based target settling. For the session workspace target, hasSelection reads only !!this._selectedFolderUri.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selection probe per displayed step attempt. The new variation has two steps; normal forward completion therefore performs two probes, with additional probes only when the user explicitly navigates back or a target is replaced and retried. Across other spotlight tours, the added global probe scales linearly with displayed steps, but each probe is a WeakMap lookup and currently the sole registered callback is a boolean property read.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Steps and retries are serialized by the presentation loop; no selection probes run concurrently and none are attached to layout, scroll, animation-frame, or input event loops.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is needed for the selection read because it is current owner state and is evaluated once when a step is shown. The same result is reused for selected copy and the existing ifUnselected open decision. Target resolution and overlay layout behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: hasOnboardingTargetSelection is a WeakMap lookup plus optional synchronous callback, and the only production hasSelection registration found reads a URI field. The call is outside recurring layout/event handlers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: User back-navigation can repeat step display, but realistic cardinality remains the small tour step count and there is no data-size-dependent callback in current registrations.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: although non-ifUnselected spotlight steps now incur one extra selection-state lookup, the mechanism is bounded O(1), not a layout read or external boundary, and is too small to establish an actionable synchronous UI regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and all diff pages. Traced startup registration, variation resolution, assignment-service cold/warm boundaries, and spotlight rendering. The PR adds fixed payload data and a constant-time selection probe; it does not add or amplify expensive boundary calls, repeated collection work, unbounded retention, concurrency bursts, or hot-path layout work. No findings or regression-fix records were warranted.
